metadata.title: The Skill Doesn't Already Know Your Data.
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: does Claude already know your company's data, or does something have to teach it first? Lands the carry-out that the skill writes your data's context into a file once, rather than reading your data automatically.
metadata.anchor_pair: N/A — source is skill-teardown format (anatomy -> pipeline -> constraint -> verdict), no anchor structure to preserve

beats.narration_text: Someone assumes Claude already reads their company's data automatically. It doesn't. It reads a file — one you write once, that spells out your data's definitions — and follows that instead.

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'Does Claude read my company's data automatically?', hesitates on 'automatically', corrects to 'once I write it down'

beats.act: 1 anatomy — a skill is a folder
beats.narration_text: This skill is called data-context-extractor. Like every skill, it's a folder Claude reads before it works, and inside is one file, written in plain language, that spells out the job: generate or improve a data-analysis skill built around your company's own data. Claude reads that file, then follows it.

shot.new_visual_element: A folder icon opening to reveal SKILL.md, references/, scripts/; SKILL.md highlighted

production_viz.label: A skill is a folder
production_viz.mechanic: A folder opens on cream to reveal three items: SKILL.md (highlighted in crimson), a references/ folder, a scripts/ folder. A caption below reads 'Claude reads it, then follows it.'

beats.narration_text: The steps run in order: read the file, work through each step exactly as written, then return the result. Nothing runs out of sequence unless a step itself says so.

shot.new_visual_element: Three-phase pipeline: Read SKILL.md -> Execute steps in order -> Return result

production_viz.label: Input in, output out
production_viz.mechanic: Three cards left to right joined by arrows: 'Read SKILL.md', 'Execute steps in order', 'Return result'. Linear, no branch points drawn.

beats.act: 3 constraint — definitions, not a live feed
beats.narration_text: What comes out is a skill built around one company's own definitions — not a general-purpose one. Feed it data or questions outside the context it was given, and there's no fallback: it still returns the same output for the same input, but only for what the file actually specifies.

shot.new_visual_element: One company's definitions filling a file; a boundary line, faint field beyond captioned 'outside the file's context'

production_viz.label: Built around one company's definitions
production_viz.mechanic: A single file fills in with rows of definitions ('active customer', 'revenue', ...), each checked off. A dashed boundary line beneath, with a faint unlabelled field beyond captioned 'outside the file's context'. Footer: 'Same input, same output — only for what's here.'

beats.narration_text: It doesn't make Claude already know your data — it writes your data's context into a skill file, once, so every analysis after that uses your definitions instead of a guess.

props.quote: It doesn't make Claude already know your data — it writes your data's context into a skill file, once, so every analysis after that uses your definitions instead of a guess.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. Give Claude a quick rundown of your own data — what your key tables and columns actually mean — and ask it to turn that into a written skill file, so every future analysis uses those exact definitions, not a guess. Liam, in for Bear.
